description: Floodplain Restoration for Salmonid Habitat in the Yakima Basin is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation developed the Schaake Habitat Improvement Project, in collaboration with several partners, to restore approximately 130 acres of floodplain within the Schaake property for salmonid habitat. Coverage: Yakima River (2023). The toolkit gives Yakima River as the location, 2023 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

Reclamation undertook this project as part of their mission outlined in the Yakima River Basin Water Enhancement Project (YRBWEP) to protect fish and wildlife through improved water management.
